---
applyTo: "_posts/**"
---

# Blog writing

- Write in English and in the first person, with an approachable, conversational voice. Be lightly playful when natural, rather than writing a chronological activity log.
- Aim for at least 60 words of meaningful prose, excluding titles, dates, captions and code. Develop the story further when sources allow; keep sparse reports shorter rather than padding or inventing details.
- Base articles on verified sources and link to them with short, readable labels. Do not invent accomplishments, motivations, feelings, opinions, intentions, outcomes or other details.
- Distinguish the author's actions from things merely observed. Mention dates only when supported by sources, label retrospectives clearly, and do not claim a pull request was merged or an issue fixed without evidence.
- Avoid filler, commentary about the act of contributing, and unsupported claims about the pace, focus, significance or frequency of work.
- Illustrate articles only when an image helps explain the subject. Use relevant images with permission, meaningful alt text and source attribution; label current illustrations when describing historical work.
